title: Misrouted fanout + config drift caused cross-region SLO breach — postmortem & action plan
creator: Ava Johnson
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-17 23:48 UTC we observed a sustained SLO breach for EU-region generation requests: p99 latency jumped from ~350ms to 1.9s and error rate increased from 0.02% to 1.8% for ~18 minutes. Root cause was a config drift in the fanout routing table deployed by an on-call change that accidentally replaced a per-region routing affinity rule with a global fallback route. This caused ~23% of EU traffic to be routed to us-east fallback pools. The sudden inter-region fanout created KV-cache cold-starts and overloaded fallback pools triggering downstream circuit breakers and priority queue starvation in the EU ingress nodes, amplifying tail latency and error counts.

Timeline and detection:
- 2026-02-17 23:44 UTC: Automated SLO alert fired for EU p99 latency >1.5s (pager to SRE on-call).
- 2026-02-17 23:46 UTC: On-call noticed cross-region traffic spike metric (eu->us-east increased to 23%).
- 2026-02-17 23:48 UTC: We confirmed a recent config change to routing-table service (manual patch) at 23:35 UTC rolled back in staging but not in prod due to a CI gating miss.
- 2026-02-17 23:55 UTC: Immediate mitigation implemented: reapply correct routing affinity, increase regional soft-capacity on EU fallback pools, and temporarily raise circuit-breaker thresholds to allow in-flight warmups.
- 2026-02-18 00:02 UTC: Metrics returned to normal; SLO alert cleared at 00:10 UTC.

Root cause analysis (why this happened):
1) Manual config change introduced a global fallback route that overrode per-region affinity; the change was pushed directly to prod via the routing service UI because the engineer believed the change was benign for global failover tests.
2) CI gating for manual prod config writes only validated schema, not semantic constraints (e.g., percent of cross-region fanout allowed, or affinity presence).
3) No guardrail alert existed for sustained cross-region routing >5% for more than 1 minute. The existing alert only tracked per-region error rates and aggregated cross-region traffic at a coarse 15-minute resolution.
4) Circuit-breaker hysteresis and queue-priority preemption were tuned primarily for local flash spikes; they were too aggressive during a sustained cross-region surge, causing premature open and cascading rate limiting for legitimate warmup traffic.
5) KV cache warmup behavior: when requests land in the fallback region the KV cache miss penalty is significant; warmed models were not carried over between pools, so fallback traffic incurred cache and kernel cold penalties that amplified latency.

Impact:
- Duration: ~18 minutes of elevated p99 latency and higher error rate for EU customers.
- Scope: ~23% of EU traffic diverted to other regions temporarily; estimated 12k requests affected.
- Business: Observed customer-facing timeouts in a handful of enterprise tenants; one advisory opened by Customer Success.

Mitigation performed during incident:
- Reverted the misrouted configuration to restore per-region affinity (owner: on-call SRE).
- Temporarily increased EU pool capacity and warmed key model caches via synthetic replay to reduce cold-start penalty (owner: infra lead).
- Adjusted circuit-breaker open thresholds to reduce sensitivity while we stabilized (owner: runtime team).
- Notified Customer Success and created a customer advisory template for impacted tenants (owner: support).

Permanent follow-up action items (owners and due dates):
1) Add semantic CI checks for routing-table writes to prod that validate presence of region-affinity rules and reject configs that increase cross-region fanout above safe thresholds. Owner: routing team (ENG-883211). Due: 2026-03-12.
2) Create a per-region cross-region-traffic alert: fire at >5% sustained cross-region traffic for 1 minute and page SRE. Owner: observability (ENG-883212). Due: 2026-03-05.
3) Harden config change path: enforce that manual prod edits require 2nd approver or time-locked push unless explicitly in emergency mode. Owner: platform (ENG-883213). Due: 2026-03-19.
4) Circuit-breaker retuning and hysteresis improvement: add workload-aware hysteresis window and backoff that considers warmup-state. Owner: runtime (ENG-884100). Due: 2026-03-26.
5) KV-cache cross-pool warmup strategy: prototype cross-region cache pre-warm for model artifacts and new request prefixes; add metrics for warm/cold miss breakdown. Owner: infra/replay (ENG-884101). Due: 2026-04-09.
6) Runbook updates: add a procedural page that covers detecting config-drift induced fanout, steps to quarantine, manual mitigation commands, and customer notification templates. Owner: SRE doc steward. Due: 2026-03-05.
7) Post-incident testing: weekly chaos test that simulates a 15% cross-region misroute to verify warmup and circuit-breaker behavior before next production release. Owner: chaos engineering team. Due: 2026-04-16.

Metrics and validation plan:
- Track cross-region traffic ratio, per-route p95/p99 latency, circuit-breaker open-count, and KV-cache miss ratio for two weeks after fixes.
- Required improvement: reduce p99 regression window to <60s for similar misroutes and ensure cross-region fanout alert pages within 60s.

Decision notes and trade-offs considered:
- We chose to temporarily relax circuit-breakers during mitigation to avoid blocking warmup traffic; trade-off is higher load on fallback pools but reduced customer latency. Long term we will implement warmup-aware backoff instead of blanket relaxation.
- Forcing two-person approval on prod routing changes increases safety but adds friction for legitimate emergency ops; we added an emergency override path with audit logs.

Owners and contacts:
- Incident lead: Miguel Ortega (miguel.ortega@redwood.ai)
- On-call SRE: Priya Desai
- Routing team lead: Chen Li
- Runtime lead: Sandeep Rao
- Observability lead: Elena Park

Follow-up tracking and next steps:
- ENG-883211, ENG-883212, ENG-883213 will be created immediately and tracked on the Regional Resilience board.
- Weekly sync for two weeks to review metrics and validate runbook drills. Owner: Miguel Ortega. Recurrence: weekly through 2026-03-31.

Conclusion:
This incident was the result of an innocuous-sounding manual routing change compounded by gaps in CI semantic validation and alerting resolution. The immediate mitigations were effective; proposed follow-ups focus on preventing repeat configuration drift, tightening detection windows for cross-region anomalies, and making circuit-breakers warmup-aware so warmup traffic is less likely to be prematurely shed.
